summary: A fluxonium quantum processor using lumped-element resonator couplers achieves a connectivity-four unit cell with single-qubit gate fidelities exceeding 99.9%, residual ZZ interactions below 1 kHz, and two-qubit RIP-gate fidelities exceeding 99% via refocused pulse sequences that suppress spectator errors. GHZ states up to five qubits are prepared with tomographic fidelities reaching 90%, demonstrating multi-qubit entanglement compatible with surface-code error correction.
motivation: Scaling fluxonium processors to two-dimensional lattices for quantum error correction requires extending qubit connectivity to four neighbors while suppressing parasitic interactions and gate-fidelity degradation from multi-qubit entanglement.
method: Fluxonium-resonator-fluxonium architecture using high-impedance ($Z > 150$ Ω), grounded lumped-element LC couplers with 2 µm niobium inductors; resonator-induced phase gates driven off-resonantly with detuning $\Delta$ from the state-dependent coupler frequencies; refocused RIP gates with $\pi$ pulses on spectator qubits to cancel conditional-phase accumulation.
result: Parallel single-qubit fidelities of 99.957(5)%, median ZZ coupling $\xi_{\mathrm{ZZ}} = 30(215)$ Hz, median two-qubit fidelity 98.8(12)% via IRB with 128 ns pulses, and three/four/five-qubit GHZ fidelities of 96.9(2)%/95.4(2)%/90.0(2)% after measurement-error correction.
